metadata.title: Linear Search
metadata.description: Implement linear search that returns the match index or -1.

instructions.main: Define `search(items, target)` that returns the index of the first element equal to `target`, or `-1` when it is not found.
steps: Loop with `for i in range(len(items)):` and test `items[i] == target`.
On a match, `return i` — the position, not a boolean.

hints.message: Define `def search(items, target):`, loop with `for i in range(len(items)):`, `return i` on a match, `return -1` otherwise.
Return the POSITION, not a boolean: `return i` gives the caller the index (1 for `search([1, 2, 3], 2)`); `True` only says 'found'.
A bare `return` hands back `None`. On a match write `return i`, and finish with `return -1` so 'not found' is a number, not None.
Check what each `return` actually sends back: `search([1, 2, 3], 2)` must be 1 and `search([], 1)` must be -1.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: Your search returns the matching index, or -1 when the target is absent.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: `search([1, 2, 3], 2)` returns the index 1 and takes two parameters.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: `search([1, 2, 3], 2)` must return the index `1` — not True, not None. Keep `return -1` for the not-found case.
`search([], 1)` must return `-1` — the not-found sentinel for an empty list.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You loop over the items with a for loop.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Search with a `for` loop: `for i in range(len(items)):`.
